Create a complete, single self-contained HTML5 file implementing an animated neon "neuron growth network" visualization with dat.gui controls. This is a brand new file (does not exist yet) — generate the full document from scratch.

STRUCTURE:
- `<!DOCTYPE html>` document, `<head>` with `<meta charset="utf-8">`, title "Neuron Growth Network", and a `<style>` block.
- Load dat.gui from CDN via a single `<script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/dat-gui/0.7.9/dat.gui.min.js"></script>` tag (this is the only allowed external library/resource).
- `<body>` contains a centered `<canvas id="canvas" width="800" height="800"></canvas>` and nothing else visible (dat.gui injects its own panel via JS, fixed top-right).
- All JavaScript in one `<script>` block at the end of body, vanilla JS only, no modules, no other libraries, no images/textures.

CSS:
- html/body: margin 0, height 100%, background `#05070f`, display flex center (justify-content, align-items, min-height 100vh), overflow hidden.
- body has a radial-gradient glow using `#101a3a` behind the canvas (e.g. background: radial-gradient(circle at center, #101a3a 0%, #05070f 70%) on body, canvas has its own subtle box-shadow glow using rgba(0,229,255,0.15) or similar).
- canvas: display block, background `#05070f`, box-shadow neon glow, border maybe 1px solid rgba(0,229,255,0.15), border-radius small.
- dat.gui panel positioned fixed top right, z-index high; a small `.dg.main` style tweak optional.
- Use font-family monospace-ish for body just in case (though nothing else visible).

COLOR PALETTE (exact hex, define as JS CONFIG constants used both for canvas drawing and as dat.gui-bound color fields):
- background: '#05070f'
- backgroundGlow: '#101a3a'
- branchColor: '#00e5ff'
- accentColor: '#d6ff00'
- synapseColor: '#ff2bd6'
- pulseColor: '#fff36a'
- uiColor: '#ffd400'
- gridColor: 'rgba(0, 229, 255, 0.08)'

JAVASCRIPT ARCHITECTURE (organize with clear comment section headers: // ===== SETUP =====, // ===== CONFIG / STATE =====, // ===== GUI SETUP =====, // ===== NEURON / BRANCH GROWTH =====, // ===== SYNAPSE DETECTION =====, // ===== PULSE ANIMATION =====, // ===== RENDERING =====, // ===== MAIN LOOP =====):

1. SETUP:
   - Get canvas + ctx (800x800), set ctx.lineCap='round', ctx.lineJoin='round'.
   - A `params` object (bound to dat.gui) holding all tunable values with sensible defaults:
     Growth folder: neuronCount (3-6, default ~4, integer step 1), growthSpeed (0.2-3, default 1 — segments grown per frame), maxDepth (2-9, default 6, integer), splitChance (0-1, default 0.25), curvature (0-1, default 0.4 — controls random angle jitter per segment), maxBranchLength (50-400, default 180 — max total length per branch chain).
     Synapses folder: synapseDistance (10-100, default 35), synapseGlow (0-40, default 18).
     Pulses folder: pulseSpeed (0.002-0.05, default 0.012 — interpolation fraction per frame), pulseFrequency (0.001-0.05, default 0.01 — chance per frame to spawn a new pulse on a random synapse), pulseBrightness (0.5-3, default 1.5 — shadowBlur multiplier / alpha).
     Visuals folder: color pickers bound to hex strings for backgroundColor, branchColor, accentColor, synapseColor, pulseColor (dat.gui addColor).
   - Buttons object with three methods: regenerate() (reset network + reseed), clearCanvas() (empty arrays, clear canvas, keep or stop growth), togglePause() (toggle a `paused` flag; also rename the GUI controller label between "Pause"/"Resume" if easy, otherwise just toggle behavior).
   - `state` object: neurons array (seed points), branches array (segments/tips), synapses array, pulses array, growing flag, paused flag, frame counter, vignette/noise helper data.

2. NEURON GROWTH:
   - `createSeedNeurons()`: pick a random int in [3,6], place near canvas center (400,400) with some random offset radius (e.g. within 60-100px), each seed neuron starts one or two initial branch "tips" with random initial angle (0-2PI).
   - Each branch tip object: {x,y (current position), angle, depth, length (accumulated length), maxLength (per-branch cap derived from params.maxBranchLength with randomness), width (line thickness, slightly randomized e.g. 1-2.5), points: [] array storing path segment endpoints/control points for drawing quadratic curves, colorMain: bool (true=branchColor, false=accentColor sometimes for secondary/side branches), alive: bool, parentId/id for tracking}.
   - `growStep()` called every frame while state.growing and !paused: for each alive tip, advance a small step length (based on growthSpeed), apply small random angle jitter scaled by params.curvature to keep organic curves, push a new point (and a mid control point) so it can be rendered later with `ctx.quadraticCurveTo`. When tip.length exceeds its maxLength or exceeds params.maxDepth via recursive branching count, mark tip as no longer growing (but keep it as a static completed branch for rendering/synapse detection).
   - Randomly (based on splitChance, checked occasionally e.g. every N steps or with small per-frame probability scaled down) spawn a new child tip at the current tip position with a new diverging angle and depth+1, if depth+1 <= maxDepth and total branch count under a safety cap (e.g. 220) to keep performance stable. Side branches spawned this way should sometimes use accent color to vary look.
   - Track total branch/tip count; once it hits a cap or all tips are no longer alive (finished/out of bounds/reached maxDepth), set state.growing = false so growth stops and the network becomes "stable"; from then on only synapse+pulse animation continues.
   - Keep tips within canvas bounds roughly (soft steering back toward center or kill tip if it goes far outside 0-800 range) to avoid wasted computation.

3. SYNAPSE DETECTION:
   - Periodically (e.g. every few frames, not every single frame, for performance) compare current tip positions (both growing tips and completed branch tip endpoints) pairwise; if distance between two DIFFERENT branches' current/end points is below params.synapseDistance, and they don't already have a synapse recorded (use a Set or a checked pair-key like `minId_maxId` to prevent duplicates), create a synapse object {a: point/branch ref, b: point/branch ref, x1,y1,x2,y2, strength (for pulsing glow, e.g. animated via sin(time)), id}.
   - Limit synapse checks to a reasonable subset (e.g. only among branch tips, not full growth trail) to keep O(n^2) small since branch count is capped.

4. PULSE ANIMATION:
   - `spawnPulse()`: with probability params.pulseFrequency per frame (only if synapses.length>0), pick a random synapse and create a pulse object {synapse, t: 0 (progress 0..1), reverse: random bool for direction}.
   - `updatePulses()`: increment each pulse.t by params.pulseSpeed each frame; remove pulses with t>=1; interpolate pulse position along the synapse's line (linear or slight quadratic bow) using lerp for smooth movement.
   - Cap total simultaneous pulses (e.g. 60) to keep performance stable — skip spawning new ones above cap.

5. RENDERING (renderFrame):
   - Clear/fill background each frame with params.backgroundColor (from GUI, default '#05070f'); optionally draw a soft radial gradient glow behind using backgroundGlow-like color mixed in (can hardcode '#101a3a' as glow base or derive) for depth.
   - Optional: draw very faint grid/scanline lines using the gridColor rgba(0,229,255,0.08), thin horizontal lines across canvas with low alpha, cheap loop.
   - Draw branches: iterate stored path points per tip/branch using ctx.beginPath + moveTo + quadraticCurveTo through stored points for organic curve; set ctx.strokeStyle to branchColor or accentColor per branch's colorMain flag (use params.branchColor / params.accentColor so GUI color pickers work), ctx.lineWidth = branch.width, ctx.shadowBlur ~ 8-14, ctx.shadowColor = same stroke color for neon glow, ctx.stroke().
   - Draw synapses: small glowing circle or short line at synapse point using params.synapseColor, shadowBlur = params.synapseGlow * (subtle pulsing factor via Math.sin(time*2+id)), alpha/brightness varying softly over time.
   - Draw pulses: small bright circle (radius ~2.5-4) at interpolated position along its synapse, fillStyle = params.pulseColor, shadowBlur = 12 * params.pulseBrightness, shadowColor = params.pulseColor.
   - Draw a faint vignette: radial gradient from transparent center to darker/black semi-transparent edges drawn last over everything (cheap, canvas-only, no images).
   - Reset ctx.shadowBlur = 0 after each glow-drawing pass segment where appropriate to avoid bleeding into unrelated draws (or manage carefully per draw call).
   - Keep all effects canvas-only, no images/textures.

6. GUI SETUP (dat.gui):
   - `const gui = new dat.GUI();`
   - Folder "Growth": add neuronCount, growthSpeed, maxDepth (step 1), splitChance, curvature, maxBranchLength.
   - Folder "Synapses": add synapseDistance, synapseGlow.
   - Folder "Pulses": add pulseSpeed, pulseFrequency, pulseBrightness.
   - Folder "Visuals": addColor for backgroundColor, branchColor, accentColor, synapseColor, pulseColor.
   - At root level (or a small "Controls"/actions folder) add three buttons via a plain actions object: 'Regenerate Network', 'Clear Canvas', 'Pause / Resume' each calling corresponding functions from step 1.
   - Open relevant folders by default (call .open() on each folder) for usability.

7. MAIN LOOP:
   - `let lastTime = 0;` use `requestAnimationFrame(loop)`; inside loop: if not paused: run growStep() while state.growing, run synapse detection periodically, updatePulses(), spawnPulse(); always call renderFrame() (even when paused, render should still show current static state — only growth/pulse updates freeze on pause, but it's fine if renderFrame also pauses, just keep it simple and consistent — simplest: if paused, skip all update logic and just keep rendering the last state without clearing/re-adding new pulses, i.e. still call renderFrame so the canvas doesn't go blank).
   - Always `requestAnimationFrame(loop)` to continue the cycle.
   - On init: call createSeedNeurons(), set state.growing = true, then start the loop.

GENERAL:
- Keep code compact but readable, with short `//` comments above each major section explaining its purpose.
- Do not reference any game, movie, brand, or copyrighted visual style anywhere in code or comments — keep all naming generic/scientific (neuron, branch, synapse, pulse, network).
- No images, no textures, no external CSS/JS other than the single dat.gui CDN script tag.
- Ensure the file is fully valid, self-contained, and runs directly when opened in a browser.
"}
